sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). Not included: technician time not charged to any job (travel, training, waiting), and overheads (office wages, marketing, vehicles, rent, insurance, IT, depreciation, interest). Profit is what's left after those. Wages include their on-costs: super (12%) and leave as it's earned. No payroll tax: wages are under Queensland's $1.3 million threshold.

Maintenance contracts: 63.9% gross margin, 28.9 points over the 35.0% target ($13,094 ahead on $45,350 in September).

Installations.shows: 2 of the 6 installation jobs invoiced in September made less than the 35.0% job gross margin target. The Wacol warehouse switchboard made a 22.7% job gross margin: 150.0 h of technician time ($10,200) and $7,400 of subcontractors on a $52,400 job. Maintenance contracts.shows: All 14 contracts made more than the 35.0% job gross margin target. The thinnest was Kangaroo Point townhouses at 62.9% job gross margin: 14.0 h of technician time on a $2,700 monthly fee.

sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). Not included: technician time not charged to any job (travel, training, waiting), and overheads (office wages, marketing, vehicles, rent, insurance, IT, depreciation, interest). Profit is what's left after those. Wages include their on-costs: super (12%) and leave as it's earned. No payroll tax: wages are under Queensland's $1.3 million threshold.

sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). Not included: technician time not charged to any job (travel, training, waiting), and overheads (office wages, marketing, vehicles, rent, insurance, IT, depreciation, interest). Profit is what's left after those. Wages include their on-costs: super (12%) and leave as it's earned. No payroll tax: wages are under Queensland's $1.3 million threshold.

All.shows: In June maintenance contracts made a 63.9% job gross margin, installations made a 36.2% job gross margin, call-outs and repairs made a 49.1% job gross margin (technician time at $68 an hour, wages and all on-costs). Jobs need 44.9% just to cover overheads.
All.action: Installations: 36.2% gross margin, 1.2 points over the 35.0% target ($1,348 ahead on $115,600 in June). Maintenance contracts: 63.9% gross margin, 28.9 points over the 35.0% target ($13,094 ahead on $45,350 in June).

Installations.shows: 0 of the 5 installation jobs invoiced in June made less than the 35.0% job gross margin target. The Installation J-2523 made a 35.8% job gross margin: 58.0 h of technician time ($3,944) and $1,200 of subcontractors on a $16,900 job. Jobs need 44.9% gross margin just to cover overheads.
Installations.action: Every installation cleared the 35.0% target. Most profitable: Installation J-2522 (37.1%).

Maintenance contracts.shows: All 14 contracts made more than the 35.0% job gross margin target. The thinnest was Kangaroo Point townhouses at 62.9% job gross margin: 14.0 h of technician time on a $2,700 monthly fee.
Maintenance contracts.action: The thinnest, Kangaroo Point townhouses: 62.9% gross margin, 27.9 points over the 35.0% target ($753 ahead on $2,700 in June). All maintenance contracts: 63.9% gross margin, 28.9 points over the 35.0% target ($13,094 ahead on $45,350 in June).

Call-outs and repairs.shows: 57 call-outs in June billed $23,723 of technician time and $8,359 of materials ($6,430 at cost plus 30%), and made a 49.1% job gross margin between them. Gross margins run from 44.5% to 51.8% by length: the hourly rate covers technician time comfortably, so the gross margin mostly moves with how much material goes on the van.
Call-outs and repairs.action: All call-outs: 49.1% gross margin, 14.1 points over the 35.0% target ($4,529 ahead on $32,082 in June).

sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). Not included: technician time not charged to any job (travel, training, waiting), and overheads (office wages, marketing, vehicles, rent, insurance, IT, depreciation, interest). Profit is what's left after those. Wages include their on-costs: super (12%) and leave as it's earned. No payroll tax: wages are under Queensland's $1.3 million threshold.

sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). sections.title: Gross margin, not profit
sections.text: Gross margin is not profit. Job gross margin = revenue less materials, subcontractors and technician time charged to the job at $68 an hour (wages and all on-costs). Not included: technician time not charged to any job (travel, training, waiting), and overheads (office wages, marketing, vehicles, rent, insurance, IT, depreciation, interest). All.shows: In February maintenance contracts made a 63.9% job gross margin, installations made a 38.6% job gross margin, call-outs and repairs made a 48.3% job gross margin (technician time at $68 an hour, wages and all on-costs). Jobs need 33.0% just to cover overheads.
All.action: Installations: 38.6% gross margin, 3.6 points over the 35.0% target ($5,224 ahead on $144,800 in February). Maintenance contracts: 63.9% gross margin, 28.9 points over the 35.0% target ($12,142 ahead on $42,000 in February).

Installations.shows: 2 of the 4 installation jobs invoiced in February made less than the 35.0% job gross margin target. The Salisbury gym air-con install made a 31.2% job gross margin: 71.5 h of technician time ($4,862) and $1,300 of subcontractors on a $20,300 job. Jobs need 33.0% gross margin just to cover overheads.
Installations.action: 2 installations under the 35.0% target, worth about $1,893 between them on $60,700 of revenue. The biggest gap, Kedron shop switchboard upgrade: 32.2% gross margin, 2.8 points under the 35.0% target: about $1,126 on $40,400 of revenue in February. It's below the 33.0% needed to cover overheads, too.

Maintenance contracts.shows: All 13 contracts made more than the 35.0% job gross margin target. The thinnest was Kangaroo Point townhouses at 62.9% job gross margin: 14.0 h of technician time on a $2,700 monthly fee.
Maintenance contracts.action: The thinnest, Kangaroo Point townhouses: 62.9% gross margin, 27.9 points over the 35.0% target ($753 ahead on $2,700 in February). All maintenance contracts: 63.9% gross margin, 28.9 points over the 35.0% target ($12,142 ahead on $42,000 in February).

Call-outs and repairs.shows: 57 call-outs in February billed $22,982 of technician time and $9,126 of materials ($7,020 at cost plus 30%), and made a 48.3% job gross margin between them. Gross margins run from 40.5% to 52.7% by length: the hourly rate covers technician time comfortably, so the gross margin mostly moves with how much material goes on the van.
Call-outs and repairs.action: All call-outs: 48.3% gross margin, 13.3 points over the 35.0% target ($4,262 ahead on $32,108 in February).
